title: Vector and Archive
premise: Sable Oyelaran, the last insurance investigator stationed on dying colony world Meridian-9, documents its slow abandonment while secretly archiving the culture of a people Earth declared extinct two centuries ago. When a distress signal arrives in that dead language, she realizes the colony's founders were survivors of a genocide Earth's records erased, and that two rival fleets are converging on Meridian-9, one to finish the erasure, one to claim it. To keep them apart long enough for the colonists' hidden descendants to escape, Sable must broadcast a fabricated proof of ownership that only her forged archive can support. In the end she burns her own credibility and career, transmitting the truth of the massacre alongside the lie that saved the living, and stays behind as the last witness when the loop finally ends.
about_author: Xanthe Iversen is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent a decade reconstructing disasters from paperwork before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast, where she collects obsolete recording formats.

chapters.title: The Actuary of Small Ends
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She files her 400th report on Meridian-9's decay: failing oxygen recyclers, a population down to nine hundred, claims no one on Earth will pay. Her private ritual, recording oral histories in an obsolete dialect, is introduced. Emotional beat: weary tenderness masked as bureaucratic detachment.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Mouth
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A repeating distress pulse arrives in Vessari, a language extinct for two centuries, from coordinates inside the colony's sealed founding vault. Sable realizes the 'extinct' language is the colonists' own mother tongue, deliberately buried. Emotional beat: vertigo, the ground of her assumptions cracking open.

chapters.title: What the Vault Kept Warm
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and elder archivist Tomas Oyelaran (her estranged uncle) POV. They open the vault together and find the genocide records: Meridian-9's founders were Vessari survivors Earth officially erased to protect a treaty. Emotional beat: grief braided with fury; family estrangement thaws over shared inheritance.

chapters.title: Two Fleets on One Horizon
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Long-range scans reveal the Concord fleet and the Reclamation flotilla both inbound, each believing the other will arrive first. The colony has weeks. Sable understands any signal she sends could trigger a war or a second massacre. Emotional beat: cold dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Forgery Lesson
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He teaches Sable the archivists' craft of authenticated forgery, how to age documents, seed provenance, build a lie with true bones. They begin fabricating a legal charter proving Meridian-9 is sovereign Vessari territory under old law. Emotional beat: uneasy intimacy; loyalty and deception entwining.

chapters.title: Auditor of Ashes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A Concord advance auditor arrives early, and Sable must play investigator against her own profession, feeding him the forged charter while concealing the vault. He half-suspects her but leaves convinced enough. Emotional beat: performance anxiety curdling into shame at how good lying feels.

chapters.title: The Loop That Would Not End
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Earth's final transmission loop, carrying the official history that justifies both fleets' claims, begins degrading ahead of schedule. Once it ends, all legal basis for either fleet expires, chaos. The escape plan must accelerate, and the forgery must be flawless by then. Emotional beat: racing clock pressure, quiet panic.

chapters.title: Everything True Is Contraband
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The Reclamation flotilla jumps in early; their commander demands the real archive as proof of bloodright. Sable must choose between handing over the truth (which dooms the descendants) or the lie (which betrays the dead). Emotional beat: moral crisis at its sharpest point.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, climax. She transmits both at once: the forged charter holding the fleets apart, and the raw genocide records attached beneath it, unencrypted, undeniable. The fleets stall, each unwilling to act while the other holds proof of shared guilt. The descendants launch. Emotional beat: terrible clarity, sacrifice made without ceremony.

chapters.title: Last Witness Standing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, resolution. The loop ends; Earth goes silent; the fleets withdraw to argue over ruins. Sable, stripped of rank and record, remains on Meridian-9 with Tomas, continuing the oral histories now openly, for whoever comes next. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, loyalty resolved into stewardship rather than secrecy.
